thermal_swing_K.detail: about 400 K by day to under 100 K by night

slope_deg.site: Site23, Malapert massif, lunar south pole (not the equator)
slope_deg.note: Site23, Malapert massif (south pole); 30 m block means of LOLA 5 m heights, 3x3 window (90 m); copied from moon_terrain.json

roughness_m.site: Site23, Malapert massif, lunar south pole (not the equator)
roughness_m.note: Site23, Malapert massif (south pole); 30 m block means of LOLA 5 m heights, tilt removed in 3x3 window (90 m); copied from moon_terrain.json

diviner_equator_K.note: additional references from LRO Diviner maps, copied from moon_thermal.json (written by pipeline/moon_thermal.py); a test checks they match. They are not used in any score: thermal_swing_K above (300 K) is still the reference.

observed_range.label: observed range across both maps, not a daily swing

second_source.note: page could not be read on 2026-11-08 (HTTP 403)

mars.detail: as given by the team; NSSDC lists 3.73 mean and 3.69 at the equator

thermal_swing_K.reason: Setting tau to the lunar swing itself makes the score the share of the Moon's swing that a site reproduces, so 0 means no swing and 1 means the full lunar swing.

slope_deg.method: sample standard deviation (n - 1) of the median slopes of the 10 km squares in terrain.json (3 sites), computed by score.py
slope_deg.reason: The spread of median slope across our three measured Earth sites shows how much this number naturally varies between Earth analogs, so a site that differs from the Malapert reference by more than that spread counts as no match.

roughness_m.reason: Tau is the Moon's own median roughness, so a gap as large as the Moon's own roughness counts as no match; the spread of only three sites (0.06 m) was too close to the 0.01 m rounding of the data to use.

mean_temperature_K.method: sample standard deviation (n - 1) of the 5 sites' mean temperatures in thermal.json, computed by score.py
mean_temperature_K.reason: The spread of mean temperature across our five Earth sites shows how much this number naturally varies between Earth analogs, so a site that differs from Mars by more than that spread counts as no match.

materials_note.method: alpha = slope of NIST's linear-expansion fit y = a + bT + cT^2 + dT^3 + eT^4, where y = (L - L293)/L293 x 10^5, taken at T = 293 K and multiplied by 10^-5; rounded to 3 significant figures
materials_note.limit: one alpha at 293 K is used for every swing; the Moon's swing (under 100 K to about 400 K) goes outside the 4-300 K fit, and alpha is smaller at cryogenic temperatures

try_it_limits.note: team choices for realistic inputs in the Try it panel, not measured data

map_bands.metric: mean day-night swing as a percent of the Moon's swing (references.moon.thermal_swing_K)
map_bands.note: team choice for the map colours, not measured data; it does not change any score

use_rules.slope_climbing_rule: a site supports slope-climbing tests at the Moon's median slope if its 90th percentile slope is at least that steep, i.e. at least 10% of its square is as steep as typical Malapert ground
use_rules.note: team choices used to write 'How engineers use it', not measured data; they do not change any score

mission_match.note: team rules for the Mission Match station: every task reuses a ranking that already exists in cards.json or the Gravity Drop formulas; no new score, tolerance or ranking

verdicts.reason: only the top two assessed sites for a task are places this atlas can point to; every other site, and every site that is not assessed, is not useful for that task

tasks.title: Climb steep slopes
tasks.reason: sites keep their existing rank by the gap between their median slope and Malapert's, and the 90th percentile slope shows whether at least some of their ground is as steep as typical Malapert ground

tasks.title: Survive big temperature swings
tasks.reason: sites keep their existing rank by the gap to the Moon's day-night swing, shown as the share of the Moon's swing each site reproduces

tasks.title: Stay as cold as Mars
tasks.reason: sites keep their existing rank by the gap between their mean temperature and the Mars mean temperature

tasks.title: Land from a drop
tasks.reason: gravity is the same at every Earth site, so no site can be ranked: an Earth drop can match the Moon's impact speed from a lower height, but never the Moon's slower fall
